candidates.exact_span: bacteria in the sewage sludge be less than three Most Probable Number per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric pathogen limit and two distinct timing triggers (use/disposal vs. bagged sale/giveaway). Different readings of which event applies to a given sludge handling action, or whether both must be satisfied, would change the enforceable limit used for comparison (A) and when monitoring or sampling must occur (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 5 and 6 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Disallows two Class A compliance pathways in Texas. Whether a facility relied on Alternative 5 or 6 affects which numeric/process requirements are enforceable (A), which monitoring or demonstration obligations apply (B), and whether absent evidence reflects a non-required pathway versus missing required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 1 - The temperature of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be maintained at a specific value for a period of time. See 503.32(a)(3)(ii) for specific information. This alternative is not applicable to composting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a process-based compliance route with an external cross-reference for the actual temperature/time values and an explicit composting exclusion. Interpretation of whether composting is involved, or what 503.32(a)(3)(ii) incorporates, changes whether Alternative 1 monitoring/temperature obligations apply (B) and how to classify periods without matching evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - The pH of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be raised to above 12 and shall remain above 12 for 72 hours. The pH shall be defined as the logarithm of the reciprocal of the hydrogen ion concentration measured at 25 degrees Celsius or measured at another temperature and then converted to an equivalent value at 25 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a numeric pH threshold (>12) and a measurement-definition rule with temperature conversion. Different readings of the pH definition or conversion method could change whether reported values exceed the applicable limit (A) and whether continuous pH monitoring during the 72-hour window was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The temperature of the sewage sludge shall be above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or longer during the period that the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a conditional temperature-duration requirement tied to the pH-above-12 period. Ambiguity about the overlap window, duration counting, or what evidence proves the condition was met changes whether temperature monitoring was required (B) and how to classify missing temperature records during otherwise qualifying periods (C).

candidates.exact_span: At the end of the 72 hour period during which the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12, the sewage sludge shall be air dried to achieve a percent solids in the sewage sludge greater than 50%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Adds a post-treatment percent-solids threshold (>50%) at a specific endpoint. Interpretation of when the 72-hour period ends or how percent solids is measured affects enforceable limit comparison for solids (A) and whether endpoint solids monitoring was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for enteric viruses prior to pathogen treatment. The limit for enteric viruses is one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Combines a mandatory pre-treatment analysis obligation with a numeric limit that may be evaluated either before or after treatment. Different readings of the allowed sampling point change the applicable limit for comparison (A), whether pre-treatment analysis alone satisfies monitoring (B), and how to treat results or absences at only one of the two permitted times (C).

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for viable helminth ova prior to pathogen treatment. The limit for viable helminth ova is less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mirrors the enteric-virus structure for helminth ova: a pre-treatment analysis duty paired with a <1 per 4 g limit evaluable at either time point. Interpretation of timing and sampling-point choice affects limit applicability (A), monitoring obligation scope (B), and classification of missing or single-point evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - The density of enteric viruses in the sewage sludge shall be less than one Plaque- forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight bas is) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a numeric enteric-virus limit with multiple operational timing triggers and contains a typographic split ('Plaque- forming', 'bas is'). Different readings of the limit unit, timing trigger, or whether OCR artifacts alter the quoted threshold could change compliance comparison (A) and when sampling was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The density of viable helminth ova in the sewage sludge shall be less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a helminth-ova density limit with the same dual timing triggers as Alternative 4 for viruses. Which event governs a given handling action affects the enforceable limit used (A) and the required monitoring window (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 5 - Sewage sludge shall be treated by one of the Processes to Further Reduce Pathogens (PFRP) described in 503 Appendix B. PFRPs include composting, heat drying, heat treatment, and thermophilic aerobic digestion.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines a process-based Class A route via incorporated PFRP methods rather than explicit numeric effluent-style limits in this span. Whether a treatment qualifies as an listed PFRP under 503 Appendix B changes which compliance standard applies (A) and what process verification or monitoring is required (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 6 - Sewage sludge shall be treated by a process that is equivalent to a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Makes compliance contingent on individual PEC approval of an equivalent process. Whether approval exists or is interpreted as satisfied changes the operative compliance basis (A), associated monitoring obligations (B), and whether missing data reflects a non-authorized pathway versus unresolved required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Four alternatives are available to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge. Alternatives 2, 3, and 4 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Enumerates Class B compliance routes while disallowing three of them in Texas. Interpretation of which Class B alternative a facility must use, or whether a disallowed alternative was attempted, changes applicable limits (A), which monitoring pathways are operative (B), and how to classify absent monitoring for unauthorized routes (C).
